title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.28947v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: NVIDIA tensor cores have supported 2:4 semi-structured sparsity since Ampere, and the pattern composes with quantization. When the two are combined, the practical question is which step to take next: from a given precision, add 2:4 sparsity or drop to the next lower precision? We compare the two at equal bits, with sparsity metadata counted, and at equal nominal tensor-core tiers, over all six GEMM operands of a transformer layer, with kernels measured on three GPU generations and online pruning and quantization included. Our results show that as long as a lower precision is available, adding 2:4 is the worse step, both less accurate and slower, because the energy that 2:4 discards from each group of four along the hardware-forced axis does not shrink with bits, while quantization error does. Once quantization reaches the lowest precision the hardware supports, 2:4 still speeds up linear layers by 1.3--1.7\x{}, and on an H100 a retrained

translated_title: 2:4稀疏还值得吗？大语言模型推理中半结构化稀疏与量化的对比
translated_abstract: 自Ampere架构以来，NVIDIA张量核心就一直支持2:4半结构化稀疏，且该稀疏模式可与量化组合使用。当两者结合时，实际问题是下一步该怎么做：在给定精度下，是增加2:4稀疏，还是降到下一个更低的精度？我们在等比特（将稀疏元数据计算在内）和同等标称张量核心层级的条件下，对Transformer层的全部六个GEMM操作数进行了比较，在三代GPU上测量了计算内核，并包含了在线剪枝与量化。我们的结果表明，只要硬件支持更低的精度，增加2:4就是更差的选择——不仅精度更低，速度也更慢，这是因为2:4在硬件强制轴上从每组四个元素中丢弃的能量不会随比特数的减少而缩减，而量化误差则会。一旦量化达到硬件支持的最低精度，2:4稀疏仍能将线性层加速1.3—1.7倍，在H100上，经过重新训练的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究系统比较了大语言模型推理中2:4半结构化稀疏与量化的取舍，发现只要硬件还有更低精度可用，降精度量化总是优于叠加2:4稀疏（后者既更不准确也更慢），只有当量化已达到硬件支持的最低精度时，2:4稀疏才能为线性层带来1.3—1.7倍的加速。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares 2:4 semi-structured sparsity with quantization in LLM inference, showing that as long as a lower precision is available, dropping precision is always the better step than adding 2:4 sparsity (which is both less accurate and slower), and 2:4 only yields 1.3-1.7x linear-layer speedup once quantization has reached the lowest precision the hardware supports.
